properties.name: Michoacán
properties.basicInfo: Michoacán is a Mexican state with various institutions working on environmental history. The Center for Research in Environmental Geography (CIGA) of the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) is in the state of Michoacán, in west-central Mexico. Founded in 2007, CIGA has a department of Environmental History, Power, and Territory, the first department of its kind in Mexico. The aim of the department was to generate social and humanistic research that differed from the socio-ecological models of other research centers in Michoacán, which were closer to the biological and ecological sciences. The department is currently led by Pedro Urquijo, a historian and geographer, and Karine Lefebvre, an environmental archaeologist. CIGA is jointly responsible for creating a bachelor's degree program in Geohistory, with a strong environmental focus, which is offered at the National School of Higher Studies (ENES-UNAM) on the Morelia Campus. The UNAM also has a humanities unit in Jiquilpan, Michoacán, where research is conducted on the environmental history of water: the Academic Unit for Regional Studies (UAER UNAM). The UAER collaborates with academic staff from the University of Guadalajara on historical-environmental issues. The Colegio de Michoacán, with two campuses—in Zamora and La Piedad—conducts research on climate history, historical marine management, and agriculture and the environment, primarily through three of its centers: Human Geography, History, and Anthropology. Its current president is a prominent environmental historian, Luis Alberto Arrioja Díaz Villaruel.

properties.name: Mexico City
properties.basicInfo: México City is the place with the largest number of universities in the country. El Colegio de México and the Universidad Iberoamericana were among the first institutions to make explicit contributions to environmental history in the country, with scholars such as Bernardo García and Alba González Jácome. Currently, the former cultivates environmental history through the Environmental History Seminar, coordinated by Sergio E. Carrera. At UAM-Iztapalapa, Alejandro Tortolero, has trained dozens of generations of environmental historians. The Centro de Investigaciones y Estudios Superiores en Antropología Social also boasts extensive experience in the discipline through the influence of Ángel Palerm, especially via Teresa Rojas, Virginia García Acosta and Antonio Escobar Ohmstede. More recently, the Centro de Investigación y Docencia Económicas has promoted environmental history through Michael K. Bess. At the Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia, stands out the Permanent Seminar on the Anthropology of Mountains and Climate, coordinated by Margarita Loera and Mauricio R. Hernández. At the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM), in the Facultad de filosofía y letras, teaching in Environmental history started in 1990 with Ignacio Sosa and Juan Humberto Urquiza. In our days there are several institutions that lead research in environmental history at UNAM, such as the Instituto de Investigaciones Históricas, where Sergio Miranda stands out, Centro de Investigaciones sobre América Latina y el Caribe, where Diana Alejandra Méndez Rojas contributes, Facultad de Filosofía y Letras, Facultad de Arquitectura, , and the Escuela Nacional de Ciencias de la Tierra, where Jahzeel Aguilera Lara conducts research at the intersection of environmental history and cultural geography; also, the Seminario de Estudios Críticos Animales and the Programa de Investigación en Cambio Climático. Finally, the Instituto de Geografía, where was developed for the first time the historical climatology by a small group guided by Gustavo Garza Merodio. At Instituto Mora, Cintia Velázquez Marroni is carrying out research in the related field of environmental history and heritage.

properties.name: Baja California Sur
properties.basicInfo: Baja California Sur is a pioneering state in environmental history research, thanks to the work of Micheline Cariño Olvera at the Universidad Autónoma de Baja California Sur since 1995. She proposed a five-strategy model for studying the relationships between the societies that have inhabited the Baja California peninsula and their marine, coastal, and desert environments. She has trained dozens of generations of environmental historians and is currently responsible for the Social Sciences Collaboratory for Sustainability (Colab) at UABCS. Thus, there is a group of environmental historians working at the UABCS Loreto campus, such as Wendy L. Domínguez; in Todos Santos, Diego Ramírez Meza, who heads the civil society organization (CSO) Proteger Todos Santos; Carlos Ibarra Meza, who contributes to the independent press outlet El Organismo; Azucena Higuera Higuera, a member of the CSO Saberes de rancho; Graciela Tiburcio Pintos, who directs the San José del Cabo–based CSO Organización para la sustentabilidad y la conservación del medio ambiente; and Diana Renée Amao, Ana Luisa Castillo, and Ivett Peña, who actively participate in the Colab.

properties.name: San Luis Potosí
properties.basicInfo: San Luis Potosí is the founding city of the Mexican Society of Environmental History. The city has two institutions dedicated to environmental history since the 1990s: the Universidad Autónoma de San Luis Potosí (UASLP) and El Colegio de San Luis A. C. (COLSAN). Environmental history at UASLP was promoted by Miguel Aguilar Robledo, a student of Karl Butzer. Historians, geographers, and anthropologists participate in its development, and its contribution to environmental history is particularly noteworthy in the training of environmental scientists. The influence of Ángel Palerm is fundamental at COLSAN, where environmental history is developed within the Water and Society Program and the History Program. Juan Carlos Ruiz Guadalajara played a leading role in the development of environmental history at COLSAN, and currently prominent figures include Sergio Cañedo Gamboa and Cleotilde Hernández Suárez. Since 2023, even without forming environmental scientists, the Environmental Sciences Division of the Instituto Potosino de Investigación Científica y Tecnológica, A. C., has played a prominent role in connecting environmental historians from UASLP and COLSAN.

Shanxi University Institute for Environmental Humanities and Disaster Governance
properties.basicInfo:
The Institute for Environmental Humanities and Disaster Governance was founded at Shanxi University in May 2024. Recognized by the Ministry of Emergency Management and the China Association for Disaster Prevention, and jointly established by the Shanxi Provincial Department of Emergency Management and the university, it is a comprehensive interdisciplinary platform for research on disaster governance and ecological civilization. It draws on the university's strengths in history, geography, ecology, environmental engineering, philosophy of science and technology, political science, and biomathematics. Its work reaches from the deep past into the present and covers disaster prevention and mitigation, post disaster reconstruction, ecological restoration, crisis response, and the building of disaster databases, with the aim of bringing research, teaching, and public service together in a problem driven school that also functions as a new style think tank.

The Institute takes history and the other humanistic social sciences as its foundation, approaching disaster through the relationship between people and nature and treating technological and humanistic approaches to mitigation as equally necessary. Its research fields include humanistic disaster reduction in China, the history of Chinese thought on disaster mitigation, the history of population, resources, and environment, the sociology of disaster, risk analysis and emergency management, climate change and social response, and the compilation of a Chinese disaster index. A publishing program is under way, including a series of comprehensive disaster histories and the journals Disaster and History and Studies in Ecological History. Alongside this, the Institute is gathering documentary material from the pre Qin period to the present for a general database of Chinese historical disaster sources, together with focused databases on major events, particular regions, and specific disaster types, and it plans to apply for major national research grants in both the social and natural sciences.

Exchange and public service are the Institute's other two commitments. It is assembling an international academic committee and organizes two or three major conferences each year, working with the Rachel Carson Center for Environment and Society in Munich, the Environmental Humanities Laboratory at KTH Stockholm, the Australian National University, University College London, and disaster research centers at several American universities, along with Chinese partners such as the Center for Ecological History at Renmin University and the Academy of Disaster Reduction and Emergency Management at Beijing Normal University. It also offers expertise and policy advice to government and society across the full arc of disaster response, and is working with partner organizations to establish a museum of disaster reduction and a laboratory for simulating historical disasters. In teaching, the Institute runs undergraduate honors tracks in environmental humanities and disaster governance, trains master's and doctoral students in disaster history, ecological history, and humanistic disaster reduction, is preparing a series of textbooks, and continues its advanced seminar on disaster and history.

The Institute has seventeen full time members from within the university, fourteen affiliated scholars, and two scholars recruited on full appointments, drawn from history, ecology, environmental engineering, philosophy of science and technology, political science, biomathematics, and economics. Affiliated scholars from elsewhere in China include Xia Mingfang, Fang Xiuqi, An Jiesheng, Wang Zijin, Wang Jiange, and Wang Shangyi, and those based abroad include Donald Worster, Kathryn Edgerton-Tarpley, and Ling Zhang in the United States, Christof Mauch, Helmuth Trischler, and Sonja Dümpelmann in Germany, Henrietta Harrison in the United Kingdom, and Fukao Yoko in Japan. Professor Xia Mingfang serves as director and chair of the academic advisory committee, with Professor Xing Long as honorary chair, Professor Ling Zhang as academic dean, Professor Zhou Ya as executive director, and Professor Han Xiang as deputy director.

Bogotá
properties.basicInfo: Bogotá has environmental historians working in three of its most important universities. Stefania Gallini created a strong group in the National University, which since she left (for Italy) is led by geographer and historian Vladimir Sánchez Calderón, who works in the Department of Geography. Claudia Leal and Shawn Van Ausdal work at the Department of History and Geography at Universidad de los Andes, and Katherine Mora Pacheco in Universidad Javeriana. They work in topics spanning cities, climate, cattle ranching, conservation and animals.

properties.name: Río de Janeiro
properties.basicInfo: Rio de Janeiro is not only one of the most important and fascinating cities of Brazil, but the center of a prolific group of environmental historians, in the country with the largest community devoted to this field in Latin America. They are housed in three major universities and work from different disciplinary perspectives. José Augusto Pádua and Lise Sedrez are part of the in the Historical Institute of Universidad Federal do Rio; Rogério Ribeiro de Oliveira and Alexandro Solórzano work in the Department of Geography and Environment of the Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio; and Dominichi Miranda de Sá and Magali Romero Sá in the Fundação Oswaldo Cruz, which focuses on studies of science and technology. These researchers from a strong network, so that anyone interested in environmental history in Latin America should consider Rio as a place of interest.
